To determine the critical exponent $p_c$ as a function of the dimension $d$, we consider the non-uniformly elliptic equation in non-divergence form:
$$a_{ij}(x)\partial_{ij}u = 0 \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^d,$$
with $I \ge a(x) \ge \lambda(x)I$ and $\lambda^{-1} \in L^p$.

In this setting, the equation has at least $d-1$ non-degenerate eigenvalues bounded away from zero from above and below (since the upper bound is $I$), while at most one eigenvalue can degenerate towards zero at the rate $\lambda(x)$. 

By analyzing the contact set via an adapted Alexandrov-Bakelman-Pucci (ABP) maximum principle, one can control the geometry of the paraboloid contact points using the $d-1$ good directions. This yields an improvement of oscillation and consequently Hölder regularity and a Liouville theorem for solutions whenever:
$$p > d - 1.$$

Conversely, by concentrating degeneracy along a line (which has codimension $d-1$, where the transversal spherical measure scales as $r^{d-2}$), one can construct counterexamples showing that the Harnack and Weak Harnack inequalities fail when:
$$p < d - 1.$$

Thus, the critical exponent is $p_c = d - 1$.

ANSWER: d - 1
